output.name: Tessum — "the Slack Line"
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the gulls flew after the sky and came home with cold in their feathers. So Ennu wove a gull from sailcloth and bone, so someone could still be seen from Vel. Halun was the first. Each evening, when the boats were out, a young woman flew it from the high rock above the harbour. A young man who wanted her rowed under the cliff, and if the gull dipped one wing toward the water, he might climb. Halun hangs in the Windward Reach, watching. A short way east, Sokul the Stooping Gull works the north ledges with its cod, and to the south, Sekál the Bone Gull keeps its short neck turned toward home. Tesuk keeps the knots to the north, and Hesk does not look away. One evening Tavo came down the sound, laughing, and tore the cloth away with the string. The girl stood on the rock until the boats came in, her hands still making the shape of a pull. Halun is up there yet, waiting for a rope that was never tugged.
output.finding: Halun lies about two-thirds of a hand-span west of Sokul, the Stooping Gull, in the Windward Reach.
